messages: liz: Heads-up — docusaurus build on staging failed after the nav migration. Linkcheck is flagging cross-page fragments as broken. Example: /guides/deploy#env-vars resolves to the page but the fragment 404s. sam: ugh. can you paste the linkcheck output? liz: Sure — pasted the relevant part below. ```text Linkcheck: 4 broken fragments - /guides/deploy#env-vars -> 'env-vars' not found in /guides/deploy (referenced from /guides/configuration) - /guides/configuration#default-cache -> fragment missing, page exists - /sdk/python#response-format -> fragment missing (used in SDK example) - /examples/cli#auth -> fragment missing after reorg ``` jia: Two common causes: 1) heading slug normalization changed (unicode/case/emoji) so old links don't match, or 2) the anchor actually lives in a different file now (cross-page refs need to point to final page). tony: Also saw this when images or code fences precede headings — some markdown parsers produce different slug output. For docusaurus you can add an explicit slug with the heading: ```md ## Environment variables {#env-vars} ``` jia: Or add an explicit HTML anchor above the heading if you prefer: `` — less pretty but deterministic. sam: Can we add a small heuristic in the linkfix script: try normalized slug variants (lowercase, strip punctuation, unicode normalize to NFKD) before marking broken? That would catch most of these without churning docs. liz: I like that. For the SDK snippet (/sdk/python#response-format) that one is from an example code block with inline heading on the next line — turning that into an explicit `{#response-format}` is safest. tony: I'll open a tiny PR with two changes: - add slug annotations for the three headings that moved - update the examples README to use absolute page links for cross-page refs PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4321 deploy-bot: CI: docs-linkcheck (failed) — https://ci.redwood/2345/jobs/7123 (logs attached) sam: Great. Once tony's PR lands, we should re-run linkcheck. Also adding the slug-heuristic in the doc tooling seems worth a follow-up. Can someone own that? jia: I'll take the link-heuristic patch. Plan: implement normalization + a fallback that searches for headings across the site and suggests the correct page. Keep it disabled by default behind a flag. liz: Perfect. Tony, can you include short changelog lines in the PR describing which pages you touched? Also add a few test links to the suite so the regressions are caught. tony: Yep. Will add tests and mark the PR as docs:link-fix. sam: One more gotcha — image-relative-paths broke in one example: `![](../assets/diagram.png)` resolved to a redirected path and the fragment logic failed. Tony, when you touch that example could you convert it to the docs assets pattern we use (static/assets/...) so it's stable? tony: Will do. liz: ETA on the PR? tony: I can get a draft up in ~45m. jia: I'll start a branch for the heuristic after Tony's PR merges so I can run against the updated snapshots. liz: Thanks folks — quick wins here. After the PRs land let's re-run the staging build and confirm linkcheck green before we merge the nav migration. :thumbsup: sam: sounds good. deploy-bot: Job queued: docs-linkcheck (rerun) -> https://ci.redwood/2345/jobs/7124 liz: tagging this thread for follow-up — will update when green.
